steps.text: Add oil, vinegar, sugar, ketchup, salt, Worcestershire sauce, and onion to a large jar with a tight-fitting lid. Shake until sugar is dissolved. Refrigerate and shake well before using.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma's Salad Dressing
raw_recipe.description: This sweet and tangy salad dressing with ketchup, oil, and vinegar is a family heirloom that has dressed many salads through the generations.
raw_recipe.name: Grandma's Salad Dressing

recipeInstructions.text: Add oil, vinegar, sugar, ketchup, salt, Worcestershire sauce, and onion to a large jar with a tight-fitting lid. Shake until sugar is dissolved. Refrigerate and shake well before using.

review.reviewBody: WOW with a few changes this recipie was the best I have ever tasted!!! so fresh and creamy delish! First of all I put used 1/2 cup of sugar not a whole cup, and I used olive oil instead of veggie oil. I put all ing. (except the olive oil) into the food processor on high until well blended. I then turned the the processor down to low and slowly in a steady stream poured in the olive oil until blended and slightly thick. all I can say is WOW my whole family raved about this salad dressing. It is truly worth a try.

I used 1/2 a large onion, 1/2 the amount of sugar and added 1 clove of garlic and a tbsp of molasses, which cut the onion flavour a bit and kept the colour rich. I took Gordon's advice and blended all the ingredients except the oil which I added slowly at the end. Very nice.

This recipe must be part of a Grandma's DNA. My Grandmother was making this when I was a kid, and I'm now 75. My only comment is about the sugar. I read several reviews and have a simple answer; the way I make it. Put all of the ingredients in a jar or bowl EXCEPT the sugar. While mixing, add the sugar a tablespoon at a time, starting with 2 tablespoons. It's easier to add than to take away. Grandmas are always right.
My family absolutely loves this recipe! It’s no problem using dried onion flakes if you don’t have a fresh onion on hand. A++++!

This was delicious, tho I did make some changes. I put all the ingredients in my Vitamix. I'm avoiding sugar, so I omitted the sugar and added 2 medium peeled oranges. I know it sounds weird, but it was good and you do NOT taste the orange. I increased the salt to 1 teas and added 1/2 teas garlic powder. I added all the other ingredients as listed, and blended it all in the Vitamix. It tasted good, but seemed bland to me. So I added the juice of 2 limes, and now I love it! Just enough tang for me. Thank you!

Made one ingredient change and that was using olive oil instead of vegetable oil. A little on the sweet side for us, so I would reduce the sugar in the future. I didn’t want pieces of onion in the dressing, so I processed this in my mini blender for a really smooth consistency. It’s a nice dressing with ingredients that are always on hand and quick and easy to make..

I like the sweet tangy taste of this dressing. We usually don't eat much sugar in this household, so I reduced the sugar in the recipe by half. I also added 1/8 teaspoon of xanthan gum, 1/8 teaspoon of pepper, and 1/8 teaspoon of garlic powder as my ketchup tasted a little flat. I also minced the onion rather than chopping it, and used Walla Walla sweet onion.

I made this for the salad bar that was part of my Christmas Day dinner. I had ranch dressing and a blueberry pomegranate vinaigrette, too. This dressing was such a hit that the other 2 weren't even opened. I made it 2 days in advance and mixed it up with my mini food processor to reduce the size of the onion pieces. A definite keeper!

Great eirhbtweaks. I made a batch but it was too sweet for my family, so I immediately made a second batch but this time without any sugar. I then mixed the two batches together, and it was much better. I stay away from veg oil and used olive oil instead. For the second batch, I was shy the required white wine vinegar contented with apple cider vinegar. For both batches, I used my blender so the onions would be pureed. I slowly added the olive oil in a thin stream while the blender was on high. As I have a huge amount of wonderful salad dressing now, I put half into a mason jar and vacuum sealed it before storing in the fridge. Thanks so much for sharing your grandmother’s recipe!

Tastes great! I used garlic infused olive oil instead of the vegetable oil. I cut back on the sugar (1/2 cup). I didn't have any Worcestershire sauce so I used a little bit of steak sauce instead. It honestly tastes great!
I pureed it in a blender and drizzled in EVOO instead of using vegetable oil. I also added 2 Tbsp of pureed horseradish to the mix. Everyone loved it and want the recipe.
I would not put sugar in the salad dressing. I would use home made ketchup instead of store bought ketchup.
Just as I remembered the salad dressing they made at our elementary school cafeteria as a kid. It's a little sweet and a little tangy. Next time I make it I'll cut back on the sugar. But I like it.
We use shallots for this

This dressing tastes exactly like the one I keep on hand for my "Spinach Salad." While this specific recipe calls for fresh onion, if you plan to store it for an extended period, I recommend using onion powder instead—along with just a small amount of garlic powder. It also tastes great with the addition of black pepper.
I used jalapeno ketchup and it gives the dressing just a bit more kick. Alternatively, hot pepper flakes or hot chili oil can also be used for more heat.

The sweet and sour flavor was delightful, and following the recipe exactly yielded perfect results. I had purchased a few bottles of white wine vinegar months ago without knowing how to use them, but now I’ve found the perfect recipe. Thank you for the inspiration.
it is very good
Just happened to be having salads for lunch today (when the recipe arrived in my email) so I made a batch. Very good, and will be making this again!
The only change I made was to use only half an onion. I made it for a salad at a church dinner and everyone raved about it. This one is a keeper!
